question: Which statement best describes Server Components are the default in app/?
options: A Server Component's logic and dependencies are NOT bundled for the browser — only the resulting HTML/serialized output is sent. Moving heavy formatting/markdown/syntax-highlight libraries into Server Components can dramatically shrink the client bundle.

Because they execute on the server, Server Components can be `async` functions and `await` data directly inside the component body — no useEffect, no client fetch, no loading flicker. Next streams the rendered result to the browser.

Anything you put in `app/` is a Server Component unless you mark it `'use client'`. It renders to a serialized description on the server, so its code never ships to the browser. You only opt into the client when you actually need interactivity.

Server Components run in a trusted server environment, so they can read the database, use server-only SDKs, and access secrets/env vars directly — no public API layer required, and tokens never reach the browser. This collapses a whole tier of plumbing.
explanation: Anything you put in `app/` is a Server Component unless you mark it `'use client'`. It renders to a serialized description on the server, so its code never ships to the browser. You only opt into the client when you actually need interactivity.

`'use client'` at the top of a file marks it (and everything it imports) as client code. A Server Component can RENDER a Client Component and pass it props — but those props must be SERIALIZABLE (no functions, classes, Dates-as-behavior). The boundary is where server-rendered data crosses into the interactive client tree.
